bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.latestActionText: Motion to proceed to consideration of measure rejected in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 46 - 50. Record Vote Number: 199.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The prior authorization model directly affects hospitals and physician groups by requiring advance approval for certain Medicare services they provide.
Third-party contractors processing prior authorization requests are typically health insurers or related entities that would lose revenue from this model's termination.
The model specifically requires enhanced technology and artificial intelligence systems for processing authorization requests, affecting technology vendors serving the healthcare sector.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Medicare pilot program that began in January 2026 in six states. The program requires third-party contractors to use enhanced technology, including artificial intelligence, to review and approve certain Medicare services before they are provided. The contractors are paid based on a share of any savings generated. This resolution would stop the program from continuing.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who deals with a federal agency.

bill.title: Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The program directly funds schools in rural counties containing federal land.
The program funds road construction and maintenance projects in affected counties.
Counties with federal land often have timber and mineral extraction activities that may be affected by resource advisory committee project decisions.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends a federal program that sends payments to rural counties containing national forests and other federal land. The money helps fund local schools, roads, and municipal services. The bill provides payments through fiscal year 2026, including back payments for 2024 and 2025, and allows counties and advisory committees to continue initiating projects through 2028.

plain.whoItTouches: People who use public land, and people who live beside it.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Motion to discharge Senate Committee on Foreign Relations rejected by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 53. Record Vote Number: 46. (consideration: CR S796)

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect deployment decisions and operational tempo for defense contractors supporting military operations in or near Iran.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to withdraw U.S. military forces from any hostilities in or against Iran unless Congress has formally declared war or passed specific authorization for such military action. The measure includes an exception allowing the United States to defend itself and its personnel or facilities abroad if attacked. It does not authorize new military operations but instead seeks to limit existing or future ones that lack explicit congressional approval.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Point of order that the measure is not entitled to expedited procedures under 50 U.S.C. 1546(a) raised against the measure agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 50 - 50. Record Vote Number: 9.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect the deployment and operational scope of U.S. Armed Forces and defense contractors supporting military operations in the Venezuela region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to end any U.S. military operations in or against Venezuela unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. It preserves the President's authority to defend the United States from an armed attack or imminent threat. The measure addresses congressional oversight of military deployments and the constitutional division of war powers.
